passage:
A farm used sensors to measure soil moisture. The system told farmers when crops needed water.
Visitors thought the sensors did all the work. The farmer disagreed. He still checked leaves, watched weather, repaired pipes, and decided when to trust or question the data.
One week, a sensor broke and reported dry soil even after rain. Because the farmer knew the field, he noticed the mistake before wasting water.
The smart farm was not a farm without farmers. It was a farm where human experience and machines worked together.
Good technology does not remove knowledge. It makes knowledge more powerful when used carefully.
